output.name: Kasveni

anatomy.part: trailing corner of the right wing

output.myth: Ennu built the first gull out of sailcloth and whale bone and gave it to Varo, a young man with no boat and too much nerve. He wanted to row out to the cliff where Tirsa sat mending nets. The sea was grey and Tavo was in a mood. Varo climbed in and pushed off. The wind took one wing and bent it, and Tavo laughed in the rigging. Varo swore at him, which Tavo liked. The gull wallowed into the swell, but its bow kept pointing at her ledge, the way a good kite points into the wind, and Varo followed its nose. He came ashore below her rocks, wet to the neck. She said he was a fool. He said the gull had chosen. She said a gull was a sensible bird and found him a dry shirt. When Varo died old, Ennu hung the gull in the Windward Reach. Its bow still points at her rocks.
output.verse:
Gull of sail and bone,
its bow still points to the rocks
where the girl keeps watch.
